ai.description: *Indotyphlus battersbyi* is a slender, 15–20 cm caecilian with a uniform dark brown body. It is distinguished by its lack of secondary annuli and a terminal shield on the tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indotyphlus battersbyi* is uniquely distinguished by the presence of a distinct, visible eye beneath the skin, unlike most other Indian caecilians which are completely blind.
ai.habitat: *Indotyphlus battersbyi* inhabits moist, leaf-litter-rich soil within tropical evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Indotyphlus battersbyi* is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows to forage for earthworms and other small invertebrates in moist soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indotyphlus battersbyi* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs in underground burrows. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indotyphlus battersbyi* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the states of Maharashtra and Kerala at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: *Indotyphlus battersbyi* is a caecilian and does not produce an advertisement call, as these limbless amphibians lack the vocal apparatus required for vocalization.
